category_title: Struggling readers who directly refuse to read
minimal_context: The student and interventionist are participating in a one-on-one shared reading session using the book 'Miss Nelson is missing!'.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's continue our shared reading of 'Miss Nelson is missing!'.

STUDENT: (Makes a reading attempt)

TUTOR: That did not make sense.

STUDENT: (Slumps back in chair with frown)

TUTOR: You wanta start this page?

STUDENT: (whispered) No.

options.A: Provide written feedback using a 3-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (needs improvement) to 3 (great job) at the end of each shared reading session.
options.B: Continuously remind the student that they are expected to participate and show effort, even if they do not know the word or are not completely comfortable with the reading.
options.C: Allow the student to select a book from several choices and use a constructivist approach to mediation, implementing scaffolds that focus on meaning and comprehension.
options.D: Ask lower-level questions focused primarily on having the student recall additional factual information about the characters, setting, or plot of the book.
